findings.explanation: ITSI writes itsi_summary, itsi_tracked_alerts and itsi_grouped_alerts itself on the search tier, so no Universal Forwarder input is involved. The ITSI Splunkbase listing is app 1841, not 617.
findings.quote: Splunk IT Service Intelligence (ITSI) — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
findings.suggested_fix: Splunk IT Service Intelligence (Splunkbase 1841), premium licence required; no forwarder-side add-on is needed for these indexes.

findings.explanation: This boilerplate tail contradicts the rest of the field and the ITSI guide. These indexes are populated by ITSI KPI searches and the rules engine, not by a forwarder modular input or a scripted poll.
findings.quote: Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the tail. State that the indexes are written natively by ITSI and that itsi_service_inventory.csv is a customer-maintained lookup.

findings.explanation: UC-13.2.10 is 'Fluentd / Fluent Bit Buffer Overflow'. KPI base-search performance and skip coverage is UC-13.2.5. The same wrong reference appears in detailedImplementation ('UC-13.2.10 focuses on KPI base search skip rate') and in prerequisiteUseCases, so readers are sent to an unrelated UC.
findings.quote: Does not replace UC-13.2.2 KPI degradation alerting ..., UC-13.2.10 KPI base search skip rate surveillance in isolation
findings.suggested_fix: Replace UC-13.2.10 with UC-13.2.5 in exclusions, in the detailedImplementation scope paragraph and in prerequisiteUseCases.

findings.explanation: The description and controlTest place itsi_searchlog in itsi_summary, but it is an _internal sourcetype (itsi_summary carries itsi_kpi and itsi_health_monitor rows). They also list 'health_score_latest >= 44' as a standalone alert condition. In the SPL, 44–56 is only the band for severity_blind_floor, and paging is driven by health_score_avg_60m <= 40/50/60.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the health lane as index=itsi_summary (source itsi_health_monitor / ServiceHealthScore) and the skip lane as index=_internal sourcetype=itsi_searchlog. State the real alert tiers: page when the 60-minute average is <= 40, or <= 50 with three low windows; warn when it is <= 60 or when the score sits in the 44–56 floor with no episodes.

findings.explanation: ITSI summary, episode and tracked-alert data is not CIM-mapped. Application_State was deprecated in CIM 4.12.0 in favour of Endpoint, and it describes process, service and port inventory, not service health scores. Host CPU/memory in Performance is not the signal this UC detects.
findings.suggested_fix: Set cimModels to an empty list (schema: none / ITSI-native indexes), or keep Performance only as an optional enrichment that is explicitly described as such.

findings.explanation: Verified status, with a generic team handle as reviewer, conflicts with SPL that cannot execute (multisearch with stats/inputlookup) and with wrong sibling references. There is no evidence of SME sign-off.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade to draft or community until an ITSI SME runs the search against a live itsi_summary index and records the sign-off.

findings.explanation: Items 2–4 are generated filler: an aggregation function 'elevating _time', 'synthetic probes' populating service_id, and an onboarding burst on itsi_searchlog are not real false-positive causes for a health-score regression.
findings.quote: Batch `avg` on `itsi_searchlog`** — Scheduled automation elevates `_time` without crossing `hs15` <= 60
findings.suggested_fix: Name real causes: ITSI maintenance windows (is_service_in_maintenance=1), adaptive-threshold retraining shifting severities, KPI base-search gaps producing N/A health, and service-template re-links changing KPI weights.

findings.explanation: Read access to ITSI service objects is normally granted through read capabilities that the default itoa_user/itoa_analyst roles already hold. Requiring itoa_admin for read-only inventory looks overstated.
findings.quote: REST polling of /services/itoa_interface/service and /services/itoa_interface/notable_event_group typically requires itoa_admin on many estates
findings.suggested_fix: Check the ITSI 'Configure users and roles' capability matrix, then state the minimum role and capability needed to read services and notable_event_group.

findings.explanation: ITSI writes these indexes internally as stash-style summary events. Operators do not control their indexing format, and TIMESTAMP_FIELDS only applies to INDEXED_EXTRACTIONS structured inputs.
findings.quote: If your NEAP emits nested JSON, flatten group_id and severity before indexing ... verify TIMESTAMP_FIELDS on itsi_summary and itsi_grouped_alerts
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the ingest-time advice and say that field names should be validated at search time (for example itsi_group_id and itsi_group_severity in itsi_grouped_alerts).

firewalled_field_flags.issue: Every multisearch subsearch contains stats (transforming), and one starts with inputlookup (generating). multisearch allows only streaming operations, so the search errors before returning rows. See https://docs.splunk.com/Documentation/Splunk/latest/SearchReference/Multisearch. Use append or union, or restructure with eventstats after a streaming multisearch.

sort 0 service_id - _time puts the newest bin first, so streamstats windows on the newest row only see that row. Because stats latest() then picks the newest row, health_score_avg_60m equals one bin and low_window_streak can never reach 3, which means prolonged_low_dwell never fires. Sort ascending by _time before streamstats.

The window names do not match the spans: health_score_avg_5m is a single 15-minute bin, and health_score_avg_15m is a 3-bin (45-minute) average. The episode lane groups by service_id and severity, while the guide documents itsi_group_severity and episodes do not carry a scalar service_id, so neap_episode_pressure is likely always null.

Application_State has no 'state' or 'info' fields and is deprecated. Performance.cpu_load_percent and Performance.mem_used live in the CPU and Memory child datasets (nodename=All_Performance.CPU / .Memory), not at the root. The search does not relate to ITSI health scores.

summary: The detailedImplementation prose gives a coherent account of ITSI health-score regression, but the short fields are template residue. The UC names the wrong collection app, points to the wrong sibling UC, maps ITSI-native data to a deprecated, unrelated CIM model, and its SPL cannot run as written because multisearch only accepts streaming subsearches.
